It then asks for h and R properly, with denominators, accounting convention and stated uncertainty, and asks the question the cycle was originally directed to ask and DESIGN dropped: whether compiled or parametric memory that survives a backbone change is demonstrated to transfer across models, which is the only external question bearing on whether SPIDER's inheritance substrate should be retrieval or parameters. established: arXiv:2608.05784v1 is a real, correctly resolved artifact. Title: 'Activity Frames: Deterministic Screen-Activity Compilation for Agent Memory and Replay'. Its own stored abstract states a Routine Overhead Ratio R of 60-343x, described by the source itself as 'a modeled upper bound', and a delegable recurrence h of 9.0% in-sample and 7.7% out-of-sample, 'for a realistic all-fleet token ceiling near 8%'. This is the source the Scout brief cited, and the single-source attribution holds: the audit independently confirmed the abstract wording from the packet's own raw evidence and reproduced the h values by re-running the producer's extractor. Evidence: raw/search_log.jsonl line 1 artifact_identity.abstract; audit.json baseline_findings[1].

The corpus those h and R figures are measured on is one professional's single-user passive pre-delegation screen-activity capture of 128,756 frames over 51 active days. This is an observation about the source's own stated scope, not a SPIDER measurement, and it is the single most important qualifier on the figures. Evidence: raw/search_log.jsonl line 1 abstract; audit.json recomputed_metrics.Q2_BOUNDING_PARAMETERS Q2_h_corpus_size_frames=128756, Q2_h_corpus_active_days=51, Q2_h_corpus_users=1.

The accounting convention for the Activity Frames overhead numbers is present in the retrieved text and was not extracted. The producer's own evidence quotes contain the all-fleet ceiling formula h(1-1/Rinfo) with the in-sample and conservative out-of-sample rates substituted ('with the in-sample delegable rate h= 9.0% it is ~9.0%, and with the conservative out-of-sample rate h= 7.7% (Section 7.4) it is ~7.7%'), the value Rinfo=343, and the section header '8.4 Limitations of the Overhead Measurements / Five limitations bound the results of this half of the paper'. The producer's characterisation of accounting_convention as 'a genuine gap in the source, not an extraction failure' is therefore false for the retrieved span. Evidence: raw/search_log.jsonl line 1 evidence_quotes 1, 2 and 4; audit.json validity_findings[9]/VF10 and probe VF-E.

In the same verified abstract, the source reports a compiled day-level prompt context block 86x smaller in 68 ms, and an agent reading that block answering questions about the day at 98.4% accuracy (Wilson 95% CI 91.7-99.7%) against an independent oracle, versus 66-80% for an LLM summary of the same capture. These are the first external comparator figures SPIDER has on record against its own observation-compression result. They are abstract-level, unreplicated, n=1, on a different substrate (passive screen-activity capture, not HTTP+HTML page structure) and a different quantity (day-level prompt block, not per-observation), and they neither replicate nor contradict SPIDER's audited 68x / 763.06-token per-observation cost floor.
